skill.name: integrate
skill.description: Guides library and implementation migrations by replacing equivalent legacy code, standardizing usage, and enforcing adoption through automated constraints.
skill.summary: Integrate new implementation approaches with code migration, consistent usage, and automated prevention of legacy patterns.
skill.author: masseater

content.value_statement: New libraries often coexist with legacy implementations, leaving inconsistent usage across a codebase. This skill guides migration, standardizes usage, and requires automated constraints against legacy patterns.
actual_capabilities: Directs migration of equivalent existing implementations to the newly introduced approach.
Requires automated constraints that prevent new code from using legacy approaches.
Identifies lint rules, types, CI, and dependency constraints as enforcement mechanisms.
Calls for one consistent usage pattern for the new approach.
Directs removal of obsolete implementations and dependencies.
limitations: Provides instructions only; it includes no executable migration tools.
Does not specify library selection criteria or framework-specific migration recipes.
Requires a host assistant with repository access to apply changes.
Does not define compatibility tests, rollback procedures, or guarantees of behavioral equivalence.

use_cases.title: Complete a Library Migration
use_cases.description: Replace equivalent legacy implementations when introducing a new library, then remove obsolete code and dependencies.

use_cases.title: Enforce a Team Standard
use_cases.description: Choose automated constraints that prevent new contributions from reintroducing an outdated implementation approach.

use_cases.title: Unify Shared Package Usage
use_cases.description: Align consumers around one usage pattern and restrict dependencies that preserve competing legacy implementations.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the integration of [library]. Identify equivalent legacy implementations, inconsistent usage, and missing automated constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate Existing Usage
prompt_templates.prompt: Integrate [library] for [purpose]. Migrate equivalent existing implementations and use one consistent pattern throughout [scope].
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: replace legacy implementations within a defined scope.

prompt_templates.title: Prevent Legacy Imports
prompt_templates.prompt: Replace [legacy library] with [new library] in [scope]. Add lint or dependency constraints against legacy imports and remove unused dependencies.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine migration with automated enforcement.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a Repository Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Migrate [scope] to [new approach]. Standardize usage, remove obsolete implementations, and enforce adoption through suitable lint, type, CI, or dependency constraints.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate migration and enforcement across a larger codebase.

output_examples.input: Review our new HTTP client integration before we expand its usage.
output: Migration gap: equivalent request helpers still use the previous client.
Usage gap: new call sites follow two different initialization patterns.
Enforcement proposal: restrict legacy client imports and retain one initialization pattern.
Cleanup proposal: remove the previous dependency after migrating its remaining consumers.

output_examples.input: What should completion mean for our validation library migration?
output: Equivalent existing validators use the new library.
New validation code follows one consistent usage pattern.
Automated constraints prevent legacy validation imports.
Obsolete validators and unused dependencies are removed.

best_practices: Define the migration scope and identify equivalent legacy implementations before changing code.
Select an enforcement mechanism that matches the language, dependency structure, and existing tooling.
Verify migrated behavior before removing obsolete implementations and dependencies.
anti_patterns: Adding a library while leaving equivalent legacy implementations unchanged.
Relying only on documentation or code review to prevent legacy usage.
Allowing multiple competing usage patterns for the same new approach.

faq.question: What does this skill help integrate?
faq.answer: It guides adoption of new libraries and implementation approaches, including migration of equivalent existing code.

faq.question: Does it include executable migration scripts?
faq.answer: No. It contains written instructions for a host assistant, not bundled migration scripts.

faq.question: How does it prevent legacy usage?
faq.answer: It calls for lint rules, type constraints, CI checks, or dependency restrictions. It names no-restricted-imports as one example.

faq.question: Is updating documentation enough?
faq.answer: No. The skill requires automated constraints because documentation and review depend on ongoing human effort.

faq.question: Does it choose the replacement library?
faq.answer: It does not define library selection criteria. Specify the intended replacement and migration scope in your request.

faq.question: Does it guarantee a compatible migration?
faq.answer: No. Compatibility testing and rollback planning are not defined in the skill and need separate project-specific safeguards.
